svg.title: ISO 1101 geometrical tolerance symbols and example callouts
svg.text: ISO 1101 – geometrical tolerance symbols, modifiers and example feature control frames
Symbols drawn as on the drawing. 'Datum' = the tolerance needs a reference (datum letter in the frame). Zone width in mm.
axis or line of a shaft
Feature control frame – how to read it
position of 4 bolt holes, zone Ø0.05 at MMC, datums A B C
flatness of a pallet locating face (two parallel planes 0.01 apart)
bore axis perpendicular to face A within 0.02
run-out of a seat to the common bearing axis A-B
top face parallel to base A within 0.01
second bore coaxial to bore A, zone Ø0.01
Order: symbol | value (Ø = round zone) + modifier | datum 1 | 2 | 3
projected tolerance zone (threaded hole + long pin)
datum feature symbol: letter in a box, filled triangle on the surface
(or on the dimension line = datum is the axis / median plane)
Example – motor-shaft style part: bearing seats A and B form the datum axis A-B
run-out of the Ø72 seat to axis A-B ≤ 0.01 mm
Measure: part in V-blocks or between centres on A and B, dial test indicator on the seat, one turn: max − min reading ≤ 0.01.
Rule: give every locating, fitting and sealing feature a geometrical tolerance; ISO 2768-2 general class only for the rest.
Axis datum: on the real drawing put the datum triangle in line with the Ø44 dimension line (shown simplified here).
